milestone: OPS-UI-P1 -- Implementation Result (Phase D, G-J, N-R)

phase_p_disposition.decision: DESIGN-ONLY. No UI code changes shipped this milestone.
phase_p_disposition.reason: The unified read model requires joining 3 separate SQLite stores (main DB, discovery corpus, wt_ops_v2) in-Python and threading new fields (candidate_role, evidence_qualification breakdown, raw_verification provenance) through operator_reader.py / operator_routes.py without risking the CONFIRMED-operator authority invariants verified in Phase L/M. A half-correct diff against a live-ish application's registry route was judged higher-risk than a fully-specified, ready-to-implement design. Per explicit task instruction: 'If not fully confident a code change is safe and correct, leave Phase P as a clearly-specified, ready-to-implement design rather than ship a half-correct diff.'
phase_p_disposition.what_IS_implemented: A pre-existing pytest test module, tests/test_ops_ui_p1_unified_read_model.py, already present in the working tree at task start (not authored in this pass), asserts the exact shape of this milestone's JSON artifacts and re-derives key numbers live against the real DBs. This milestone's three artifacts were written to satisfy that pre-established contract, and the suite was run to confirm.

ready_to_implement_spec.new_method: fetch_unified_investigation(self, entity_or_operator_id: str) -> dict -- read-only, joins operators/operator_entities (wt_ops_v2.db) + creator_funders (flex_complete_database.db, separate connection) + candidate_families/candidate_family_members (local_operation_discovery_corpus.db, separate connection); returns the 8-dimension structure specified in phase_c_unified_read_model_spec of ops_ui_p1_unified_operations_read_model.json.
ready_to_implement_spec.new_route: GET /api/ops/operators/<operator_id>/unified (or /api/ops/investigation/<entity_address>/unified for pre-candidate entities without an operator_id) in operator_routes.py, delegating to the new reader method.
ready_to_implement_spec.template_change: operators_index.html summary card: add a secondary, visually de-emphasized 'evidence qualification' line (e.g. '23 HIGH / 82 valid / 18 historical-only of 123 historical') beneath the existing primary count, hidden entirely when no discovery-corpus match exists for that operator (so CONFIRMED operators like WATCHTOWER/3SW2 render exactly as today unless corpus data actually links to them).
ready_to_implement_spec.safety_gate_before_shipping: Must add a unit test asserting the new route/method never writes (grep for .execute with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against operators/operator_entities/creator_funders/candidate_families, same guard pattern as test_no_production_write_statements_in_this_test_module in the existing suite) before this is merged.

phase_d_summary_card_design.principle: Historical population count stays PRIMARY and unchanged in size/prominence for every investigation. Evidence qualification is a secondary, smaller-type breakdown line, shown only when it differs from the historical count (i.e. never shown as a redundant restatement for a fully-qualified population).
phase_d_summary_card_design.generic_rule: Card renders: [PRIMARY] historical_launches count (source: creator_funders) -- always shown, always the historical figure, never replaced by a qualified subset. [SECONDARY, muted] 'N HIGH / M valid / K historical-only' breakdown -- shown only if discovery-corpus classification data exists for that entity. [BADGE] canonical_operation YES/NO. This rule is generic and entity-agnostic: it was NOT special-cased for Dv34's specific numbers, and applies unchanged to WATCHTOWER (69 entities, all canonical, no need for a qualification line to appear differently) and to any future investigation.
phase_d_summary_card_design.confirmed_operation_rule: For CONFIRMED operators (WATCHTOWER, 3SW2), canonical counts (entity_count, treasury/creator/client breakdown from operator_entities) remain the PRIMARY and ONLY prominent numbers; any evidence-qualification data is rendered as a small secondary chip, never replacing or reordering the canonical numbers.

phase_g_detail_view_design.Overview: IDENTITY + AUTHORITY dimensions from the unified read model; historical vs qualified counts per Phase D card design, larger.
phase_g_detail_view_design.Evidence: operator_evidence rows (existing) + EVIDENCE_QUALIFICATION dimension (classification breakdown, raw_verification_status) shown together, each row provenance-labeled by source (MAIN_DB / DISCOVERY_CORPUS / RAW_VERIFICATION_LEDGER).
phase_g_detail_view_design.Members: operator_entities (existing) merged with candidate_family_members where a corpus link exists; every member row shows entity_type AND, where applicable, its NON-ATTRIBUTIVE INFRASTRUCTURE marking (never removed, always labeled).
phase_g_detail_view_design.Funding_Lineage: CEX/INFRA -> private intermediary -> creator -> token chain rendered from FUNDING_TOPOLOGY dimension (direct_funding_edges + upstream_edges + root_cex_infra_category); infrastructure nodes marked NON-ATTRIBUTIVE INFRASTRUCTURE, never removed from the chain.
phase_g_detail_view_design.Analysis: BEHAVIOURAL_TOPOLOGY_EVIDENCE dimension: funding mechanisms, recurring amounts (exact_amount_repeats), timing, migration_signer_reuse vs create_creator_reuse shown as two structurally separate fields, candidate subfamilies (composite_families linkage).
phase_g_detail_view_design.History: existing operator_reviews + operator_promotion_history timeline, with new discovery/evidence events APPENDED (never replacing prior entries), tagged with the source badges from Phase F (NEW_DISCOVERY / EVIDENCE_UPGRADE / RAW_VERIFIED / etc).

phase_h_provisioner_representation.model: provisioner -> creator -> launch is always representable as a funding-topology chain (FUNDING_TOPOLOGY dimension), independent of whether any operation identity exists. provisioner -> candidate_operation is a SEPARATE, optional edge that only exists if independently established (>=2 independent identity-class evidence signals per canonical_merge_contract.py) -- never inferred merely from shared provisioner funding.
phase_h_provisioner_representation.dv34_application: Dv34 is represented purely as a PROVISIONING_NETWORK_CANDIDATE: the provisioner->creator->launch chain is fully populated (123 historical relationships), but no provisioner->operation edge exists because no independent operation-identity evidence beyond shared funding lineage (SHARED_SOURCE_LINEAGE with WATCHTOWER) has been established. This is the explicit lesson encoded in canonical_merge_contract.py's B48k/Dv34 discussion and is preserved, not overridden, by this read model.
phase_h_provisioner_representation.cardinality_rule: A provisioner may support one, multiple, or zero coherent operations; the read model never merges launches merely because a provisioner is shared.

phase_i_cex_view_integration.existing_cex_view: templates/ops_tokens.html, backed by src/core/operation_dashboard_routes.py (e.g. GET /api/ops-v2/cex-funding-intelligence). This is the SAME older wt_ops_v2-backed dashboard flagged in Phase A as distinct from the live Operations registry -- confirmed by direct grep, not touched or modified.
phase_i_cex_view_integration.integration_design: Add a contextual outbound link/button on the Operations investigation detail page's Funding/Lineage tab, e.g. 'View CEX funding intelligence for this entity ->' linking to the existing /ops-v2 cex-funding-intelligence view filtered by the current entity address. No CEX dataset is duplicated, re-queried, or re-rendered inside Operations; only a navigational link is added.
phase_i_cex_view_integration.not_implemented_this_pass: The link itself is design-only (Phase P disposition applies); adding it is a single-line template change once the detail-view route exists.

phase_j_conflict_presentation_examples.dv34_example: Historical relationship: YES (123 in creator_funders) / Evidence qualification: 23 HIGH, 82 valid-not-HIGH, 18 historical-only / Raw verification: 6/6 VERIFIED (sample) / Human authority: DV34_OPERATION_IDENTITY_PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, not canonical.
phase_j_conflict_presentation_examples.generic_negative_example: Historical relationship: YES / Evidence qualification: LOW / Raw verification: NOT PERFORMED -- rendered exactly as-is, never collapsed to a single verdict.
phase_j_conflict_presentation_examples.generic_contradiction_example: Historical relationship: YES / Raw verification: CONTRADICTED / Human authority: UNRESOLVED -- both sides always visible; the read model has no code path that hides either source (verified structurally by test_conflict_presentation_rule_documented and test_authority_state_never_derived_from_evidence_qualification in tests/test_ops_ui_p1_unified_read_model.py).

phase_n_read_projection_placement.chosen_layer: src/ops/operator_reader.py (new method fetch_unified_investigation), the SAFEST existing read layer -- already read-only, already the sole consumer of OPS_DB_PATH for the registry, already pattern-matches 'connect, SELECT, join in Python, return dict'.
phase_n_read_projection_placement.cross_db_read_pattern: Three independent sqlite3.connect(f'file:{path}?mode=ro', uri=True) calls (wt_ops_v2.db, flex_complete_database.db, local_operation_discovery_corpus.db), each queried and closed separately, results merged as plain Python dicts. No ATTACH DATABASE statement anywhere in the design.

phase_o_performance_measurements.method: time.perf_counter() around real sqlite3 queries against the actual live database files in this repository, executed directly in this session (not simulated).

measurements.query: list_operators (SELECT * FROM operators WHERE status != 'REJECTED' ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 100)
discovery corpus classification funnel (GROUP BY classification)
Dv34 historical population count (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM creator_funders WHERE funder_address=?)

query_plan_verification.query: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT COUNT(*) FROM creator_funders WHERE funder_address=?
query_plan_verification.plan: SEARCH creator_funders USING COVERING INDEX idx_creator_funders_funder (funder_address=?)
query_plan_verification.verdict: Index-backed, NOT a full table scan. Confirms Phase O requirement to avoid scanning the 1.9M token rows / 4.97M transfer rows tables -- creator_funders lookups by funder_address use a covering index and complete in single-digit milliseconds regardless of table size.

phase_o_performance_measurements.conclusion: All measured read paths are sub-10ms on the actual live DB files. No unbounded graph traversal was exercised (funding-topology hop queries were traced in code but not benchmarked at depth >1 this pass -- flagged as an open question below). No query loads the full 1.9M-row token table or 4.97M-row transfer table.

phase_r_live_rendering.decision: SKIPPED live Flask rendering; relied on direct function/query testing instead.
phase_r_live_rendering.reason: Starting the full Flask app risked touching live-ish shared state (schedulers, DB write serializer, WAL) documented as fragile in this repository's own operational history (see MEMORY.md: listener conn leaks, lock storms, WAL pinning). Given ZERO new routes were actually wired this pass (Phase P is design-only), there is no new route to render. Direct sqlite3 queries against the real DB files (as used throughout this artifact) were judged sufficient and lower-risk evidence.

verdict_reasoning: The unified read model is fully specified, traced against real repository code, and validated against real data (Dv34 123/23/82/18/6:6, Watchtower and 3SW2 controls both confirmed unmutated, discovery corpus 385/8 verified live, performance sub-10ms and index-backed). No source-authority conflict was found that needs human resolution (Phase B cleanly separates canonical vs workflow vs UI-filter states using only existing enums), and no performance problem was found. However, actual UI/route code was deliberately NOT shipped this pass because doing so safely requires touching operator_reader.py/operator_routes.py -- files backing a live-ish registry -- and the task explicitly authorizes leaving Phase P as a ready-to-implement design when not fully confident in a diff's safety. Human review of the ready_to_implement_spec before wiring the new route/method into the live app is the recommended next step.
open_questions_for_human: Should the strict intake queue threshold be STRONG_CANDIDATE_FAMILY x ATTRIBUTABLE (8 families) or the broader STRONG+PARTIAL context tier (102 families)? This design used 8 as the default queue and 102 as background context; confirm that split matches analyst expectations.

Funding-topology hop queries beyond depth 1 (upstream_edges chains) were traced in code but not benchmarked at realistic depth/fan-out this pass -- recommend a follow-up performance pass before wiring a multi-hop lineage view into a live detail page.
The InvestigationLifecycleService <-> local_operation_discovery_corpus.db family_id wiring gap (Phase F) needs a small adapter; not yet built, flagged as the concrete next implementation step.

Whether operator_reader.py is the right long-term home for fetch_unified_investigation(), or whether a new src/ops/unified_investigation_reader.py module would keep operator_reader.py's existing surface simpler -- both are safe; this design chose reuse over a new file, open to reconsideration.
